name: Earl Whitaker

five_sec.what_is_it: Something that texts the family supper ideas and makes a grocery list. Like what the lady at church talked about.
five_sec.who_for: Families with young folks who order groceries on the phone.
five_sec.trust_why: It says no card, and it says right out 'We don't deliver food.' But 'Powered by Instacart' and 'cart' is store-ordering talk I don't use.
five_sec.next_step: Read on down slow before I touch that green button. Probably show Brenda.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The dark green line 'We don't deliver food. We plan your week and send your grocery list.'

full_page.what_stopped_me: Two plans, a free one and a $4.99 one with '14 days' on it. Every time somebody says free for 14 days, they want money on day 15. And it's all about putting things in a Walmart or Instacart cart on the phone. I drive to the Walmart and push a real cart.
full_page.whats_missing: Whether I can just get the list on paper or a text and take it to the store myself. Something up top about sugar, not just a little 'Diabetic-friendly dinners' link way down at the bottom. Whether the boys will eat what it picks for Brenda.

DD.quote: It says 'no card' three or four times and has a lady's name, Sarah. That's more than most. But what's a Walmart cart in my phone?

five_sec.what_is_it: A phone app with pictures of food. Not sure what it does.
five_sec.trust_why: The big orange button is 'Letter from the CEO.' Why would I want a letter from a CEO? And it's a picture of an app, which I don't do.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The phone shows a rice bowl and pancakes on a 'Your Menu' screen. Could be a restaurant ordering thing for all I know.

full_page.what_stopped_me: 'Ollie uses AI' right there in the questions, and 'prices are available when you download the app.' That's two of my no's in one line. The price page says $25 a month.
full_page.whats_missing: Anything about diabetes. A plain price. A way to use it without an app.

OL.quote: They won't even tell you the price till you download their app. No sir.

five_sec.what_is_it: Something about dinners. 'Less Stress, More Dinners' and a video.
five_sec.who_for: Mothers with little girls, from the picture.
five_sec.trust_why: Looks like a real company, been around a while, but it doesn't say what it costs.
five_sec.next_step: Scroll a little. I'm not watching a video.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: There's a picture of a phone with food all round it. Could be either way.

full_page.what_stopped_me: A box popped up asking for my email to 'Unlock This Special Offer,' and 'Try Free for 14 Days' everywhere with no price. That's a trial. Trials charge you.
full_page.whats_missing: The price. I did see 'Low Carb' and there's a Diabetic plan on the other page, which is more than the others said about sugar.

EM.quote: They got a diabetic plan, I'll give 'em that. But 'Try Free for 14 Days' and no price anywhere. I know how that goes.

five_sec.what_is_it: A game of some kind. 'Open A Box To Reveal Your Offer.' Then it's food boxes.
five_sec.who_for: Folks with money to spend on boxes of food.
five_sec.trust_why: Pick-a-box is how the fair takes your money.
five_sec.next_step: Hit 'Continue Without Offer' and probably leave.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The boxes with HelloFresh on them and plates of food behind.

full_page.what_stopped_me: It wants my zip code before it'll say a price, and the little print at the bottom says 'auto-renewing subscription.' Bacon, pork, cheese on everything. Not on our money.
full_page.whats_missing: A price I can see. Anything for a sugar diet my wife can trust.

HF.quote: Pick a box to see your offer. That's a carnival game, not supper.

five_sec.what_is_it: A recipe app. 'Recipes, Meal Plans and Grocery Lists, All in One App.'
five_sec.who_for: Folks who keep a lot of recipes on their phone.
five_sec.trust_why: Says no card. But the first thing on the screen is two app store buttons.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Picture's of somebody writing in a notebook. It's about lists.

full_page.what_stopped_me: It's an app, and after 14 days it's $5.95 a month. And it saves recipes you find online. I don't find recipes online, I get 'em from Brenda's box. There's a '50% OFF' clock counting down at the bottom too.
full_page.whats_missing: It doesn't pick the suppers for you. Nothing about diabetes I could see.

PTE.quote: It's for people who already got recipes saved on the phone. I need somebody to tell me what to cook.

dd_offer.why: It says no card plenty, but there's a free plan and also 'Family free for 14 days' and '$4.99/mo.' Two plans and a countdown confuse me. I'd need Brenda or one of the boys to tell me which one I'm on.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: I figure they'll start charging me $4.99 a month, or keep pestering me till I give them a card.

head_to_head.reason: It's the only one that said plain it don't bring food, don't want a card, and has a real woman's name on it.

OL.reason: Ollie says AI and wants an app. DinnerDrop works from the website and texts.

EM.reason: eMeals has a diabetic plan, but it's a trial with no price. DinnerDrop says $0.

HF.reason: HelloFresh sends boxes we can't afford and hides the price behind a zip code.

PTE.reason: Plan to Eat makes you find your own recipes and is an app that costs after two weeks.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page, right under 'Start free, no card needed': one plain line that I can just print or text myself the grocery list and take it to Walmart in person, plus that the free plan never turns into a bill. All the cart talk makes it sound like it's only for people who order on the phone.
